items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: I had a fellow here named Augustine. He was a trombone player. He come from Memphis.

ctx.x: No? I had a fellow here named Augustine. He was a trombone player. He come from Memphis. He was one of the first I saw after I saw this fellow do it downtown, the loop. But it's easy. You can't press your loop too hard. Just let it loose, see, and practice getting your note what you're going to start on and then let your loop loose and then that third comes right in, see, follows it up. I had a lot of experience on those things,

see. What about pressure? For a while, it was a fad they use, as they say, no pressure at all. I've seen people in the demonstration of a trumpet hanging up on a string and walked up to it without touching it and hit a high C without any pressure. Without any pressure. Yes, I don't know what I'm saying.
